BIGGEST LESSON I’VE LEARNED

COMMUNICATING DATA MEANINGFULLY

THE ANALYTICS ARE THE EASY PART

COMMUNICATING RESULTS IS THE HARD PART

 AND MAKE IT LOOK HARD

IT’S HARD TO TAKE A COMPLICATED IDEA
 AND MAKE IT LOOK SIMPLE

 (THAT’S GREAT TEACHING)

Web APIs to Share Data
Web APIs to Share Data

OPEN DATA:
 • Many countries, states, cities, counties are
 publishing data (by law) under open data
 initiatives.

 • Data on an unbelievable variety of governmental
 activities are available.

 • Increases transparency and accountability and
 ultimately enhances democracy.

 • Allows for improved services as deficiencies are
 surfaced.
BED BUGS IN BOSTON:
BOATING ACCESS SITES IN OREGON:

APIS POWER THE WEB:

 • API: Application Programming Interface.

 • “An API isn’t the same as the remote server —
 rather it is the part of the server that receives
 requests and sends responses.”

 • APIs are the efficient way to separate concerns.

 • Serve data to visualizations (both your own and
 to 3rd party developers)

APIS POWER THE WEB:
 • Often return data in a format called JSON.

 • More flexible than csv/tabular data formats.

Dogfooding

 Eat your own down food

 A slang term used to reference a
scenario in which a company uses its
 own product to test and promote the
 product.

Dogfooding is about
 creating a virtuous
 cycle.

DASHBOARDS OR SUMMATIVE RATINGS

 • Why not both?

 • With a robust API serving your data, you (and
 others) can build reports/visualizations around
 that data.

 •

LESSONS LEARNED

 • Separate data preparation from data
 visualization.

 • Build modern web-services to serve data.

 • Watch a thousand flowers bloom.
